title: Zoom account and client ids, documentation placeholders and masked token values
summary: An account id and client id in a token request, the grant type and expiry, and an access_token, Bearer or refresh_token value that is the documentation placeholder, an environment reference or a masked display.
rationale: The account id and client id are public identifiers, and the grant type and expiry are not the token. A placeholder or reference stands in for a value kept elsewhere, a documentation placeholder for a token is not a token, and a masked display has no recoverable value. Protecting any of these would redact text a reader needs.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: the values here are identifiers, placeholders, references, masked text or non-secret outputs, not credential values. That a placeholder or reference is not a value is a project decision, not a Zoom statement.

sources.supports: Use the account_credentials grant type to generate an access token.
Refresh tokens expire after 90 days. You should always use the latest refresh token for the next refresh request.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
